issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, so IDs containing slashes or reserved characters call the wrong endpoint.
Pagination has no repeated-cursor or page-count guard, so a bad API response can cause an infinite request loop.
List responses use loose get/skip parsing, allowing malformed or missing items fields to produce incomplete results instead of a client error.
batch_create silently ignores non-object result entries and does not validate result count or indices, which can hide dropped task creations.
Transport-level httpx failures are neither retried nor wrapped in LumenAPIError, so callers must handle undocumented exception types.
Retry-After only supports numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date values, potentially retrying earlier than the server requested.
max_attempts is not validated, so zero or negative values skip the request and raise a misleading generic API error.
Model parsers coerce and trust API values without runtime validation of required types or Literal enum values.
Boolean parsing uses bool(value), so string values like "false" would be interpreted as true.
Frozen dataclasses expose mutable dict fields directly, undermining immutability and allowing caller-side mutation after construction.
batch_create eagerly materializes the entire input iterable, which contradicts the any-number-of-tasks claim and can exhaust memory on large streams.
Tests cover happy paths and basic retries but omit negative coverage for encoded IDs, malformed responses, repeated cursors, and transport errors.
